items.title: Bob Lovett Interview, 1949-04-01
items.q: And there was a piano player named Paul Jackson and a banjo player named Paul Boeberg and Jack Seldon on drums.

ctx.x: G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Was Gerald behind the formation of the jazz group at Chipoga?

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Well, Dan was playing with what members of it were here then. He was here a year or so before I came here. And after I came here, he sort of became interested in other things. And Jack Selden became the drummer.

G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Jack Selden was from Texas, is that right? G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. And I remember him going back and I corresponded with him years later, but I hadn't heard of him in recent years. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. That is maybe in mid-50s or something. I don't know if we had an exchange or two. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Yeah. G-E-R-O-U-L-D. Now in 49, you came to, 48 rather, you came to the University. And do you remember who made up the first groups that you played with? Was it then called the…
